articles.title: Italy becomes latest country to withdraw support for Infantino ahead of March 2027 FIFA election
articles.summary: Football News: Italy's football federation pulls support for Gianni Infantino's FIFA presidency, joining a wave of European opposition. The FIGC's decision reflects growing dissent over FIFA governance and international competition management, as Infantino's leadership faces scrutiny ahead of the 2027 election.
articles.body: Gianni Infantino's bid for another term as FIFA president has suffered another setback after the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) withdrew its support for his candidacy, adding Italy to a growing group of European federations turning against the FIFA chief.The FIGC announced the decision on Wednesday, August 26, saying it would no longer support Infantino in the FIFA presidential election scheduled for March 2027.Italy breaks with InfantinoThe FIGC said its decision was made in agreement with UEFA and its president, Aleksander Čeferin, and was directly linked to Infantino's recent initiatives concerning the governance and development of international competitions.In its official statement, the Italian federation said:“The Italian Football Federation has decided to withdraw its support for Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for the FIFA presidential election scheduled for March 2027.”The FIGC added that the move was intended to “clearly and transparently express” its position regarding the FIFA president's recent initiatives.FIGC president Giovanni Malagò said Italy would continue working with UEFA and other European federations around a model of football based on “merit, solidarity, sustainability, and the centrality of fans.”He added that the federation identified with a system of “dialogue, listening, and shared responsibility”, which he said had allowed football to develop while protecting its founding principles.The World Cup investment plan triggered the backlashInfantino has faced mounting opposition since his controversial proposal to allow private investors to buy stakes in the commercial rights to FIFA competitions, including the men's World Cup.The plan was ultimately abandoned, but the controversy has developed into a much broader dispute over FIFA's governance and the way international competitions are managed.According to The Associated Press, three continental confederations have accused Infantino of “deception”, while UEFA has threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions.The Italian federation's decision therefore comes as part of an increasingly organised European backlash rather than as an isolated withdrawal of support.England, Ireland, Wales and Scotland had already withdrawn their backing for Infantino's reelection earlier this month. Norway has also called for him to step down, while Norway joined Sweden, Finland, Denmark, Iceland and the Faroe Islands in saying they had “lost confidence” in his leadership.Romania also withdrew its support on Wednesday, with the Romanian Football Federation's executive committee voting against backing Infantino for another mandate.FRF president Răzvan Burleanu said:“FIFA needs today a new leader who can produce consensus and unity, inspire trust and who has the ability to bring us all together.”Infantino's once-uncontested reelection is now under pressureThe scale of the opposition marks a significant change from the position Infantino appeared to occupy before the controversy erupted.He has served as FIFA president since 2016 and had previously appeared likely to secure reelection without serious opposition at next year's election in Morocco.That picture has now changed considerably.FIFA has set November 18, 2026 as the deadline for challengers to submit their nominations ahead of the March 2027 election.While several European federations have publicly withdrawn their support, Infantino still retains backing from some FIFA member associations.Among those publicly supporting him are Morocco, one of the hosts of the 2030 World Cup, as well as Qatar, where Infantino lived before the country hosted the 2022 World Cup, and Lebanon, which granted him citizenship earlier this year.Saudi Arabia, which will host the 2034 World Cup and has close ties with Infantino, has not publicly backed him.For now, Italy's decision adds another major European federation to the opposition camp and further complicates Infantino's attempt to secure another term.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England star Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving, nitrous oxide possession after Lamborghini crash
articles.summary: Football News: England football star Raheem Sterling is facing serious charges after a single-vehicle Lamborghini crash, including dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide. He is set to appear in court on September 15, 2026.
articles.body: Raheem Sterling has been charged with dangerous driving following a single-vehicle collision involving a Lamborghini on a motorway in southern England.The former England winger is also facing charges relating to the possession of nitrous oxide (laughing gas), for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen. No other vehicle was involved in the incident and no injuries were reported.Sterling is due to appear at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court on September 15.Charges follow May motorway crashThe charges stem from an incident on the M3 southbound near the Minley Interchange in Hampshire on May 28, 2026.According to the Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary, Sterling, 31, was driving a Lamborghini when it was involved in a single-vehicle collision.The force said Sterling had been charged with:Dangerous drivingPossession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalationFailing to provide a specimenThe Associated Press reported that Sterling had initially been arrested following the crash and subsequently released on bail while police continued their enquiries.Police had previously suspected Sterling of driving a vehicle while unfit through drugs, although that suspected offence has not been included among the charges he now faces.A source close to Sterling told BBC Sport in May that there was “no proof” of drugs being present in his system.The same source said Sterling had endured “an extremely tough couple of years”, claiming he had been made to feel “worthless” and “forgotten about.”The police confirmed that the collision involved no other vehicles and that nobody was injured.Sterling's next court dateSterling will now have to appear before the court on September 15, where the charges will be addressed.The Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary confirmed the hearing date and the three charges against him.The case comes at a difficult point in Sterling's playing career, with the 31-year-old currently without a club.Sterling is currently a free agentSterling most recently played for Feyenoord, joining the Dutch club on a short-term deal in February after leaving Chelsea by mutual consent.He made eight appearances for Feyenoord before the arrangement ended at the conclusion of last season.His departure from Chelsea followed a difficult period at Stamford Bridge.Chelsea signed Sterling from Manchester City for £47.5 million in 2022, but after returning from a loan spell at Arsenal in the 2024-25 season, he was subsequently excluded from Chelsea's first-team plans and made to train separately.Sterling had spent seven years at Manchester City, winning four Premier League titles, five League Cups and one FA Cup before making the move to Chelsea.His career had begun at Queens Park Rangers, from whose academy he progressed before joining Liverpool. He made his senior debut for Liverpool and moved to Manchester City in 2015.A distinguished England careerSterling also enjoyed a substantial international career.He won 82 England caps between 2012 and 2022, appearing at three World Cups and two European Championships.He scored 20 goals for England, helping Gareth Southgate's side reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the Euro 2020 final.Away from football, Sterling has also been recognised for his work addressing racism and discrimination in sport. He was appointed an MBE in the 2021 Queen's Birthday Honours for services to racial equality in sport, following his campaigning and outspoken work against racism both within football and more broadly.For now, however, Sterling's immediate concern is the legal case arising from the May collision. He remains without a club and is due in court in September, with the charges yet to be determined.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: UEFA ready to drop FIFA boycott threat after assurances private World Cup sell-off plan won’t return
articles.summary: Football News: UEFA prepares to lift its threatened boycott against FIFA after receiving assurances that the controversial selling of World Cup stakes to private investors will not be revived. This decision aims to ensure that upcoming FIFA tournaments proceed without disruption, although pressure on FIFA President Gianni Infantino continues to escalate.
articles.body: UEFA is reportedly ready to call off its threatened boycott of FIFA competitions after receiving assurances that Gianni Infantino's controversial plan to sell stakes in the World Cup and other major tournaments to private investors will not be brought back.The decision would prevent the dispute from spilling into upcoming FIFA tournaments, but it does not appear to signal an end to UEFA's confrontation with Infantino, whose position has come under increasing pressure across European football.How the boycott came aboutThe row erupted after FIFA's proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors became public.UEFA and all 55 of its member associations responded by taking an unusually hard line, agreeing to boycott FIFA tournaments in protest.In a joint statement earlier this month, UEFA said:“UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.”FIFA eventually withdrew the proposal in July, but UEFA wanted more than simply seeing the plan disappear. The European body also sought assurances that a similar attempt to sell stakes in the sport's biggest competitions would not be revived.That now appears to be the key reason the boycott is being reconsidered.UEFA ready to lift the threatAccording to Reuters, sources familiar with the discussions said Wednesday that UEFA is set to drop its boycott after receiving assurances that the investment plans will not return.UEFA officials are expected to tell FIFA's executive committee and the presidents of most of its member associations at a meeting in Monaco on Thursday that the conditions required to lift the boycott have been met.The first FIFA tournament that could have been caught up in the dispute was the Under-20 Women's World Cup in Poland, which is due to take place next monthThat tournament now appears to be safe from the standoff. A FIFA spokesperson told Reuters:“FIFA is pleased that all qualified teams will be participating in the upcoming FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup.”The spokesperson added:“FIFA strongly believes that football has the power to unite, even in challenging circumstances, and looks forward to welcoming all teams and players to Poland.”FIFA also said:“We remain committed to how we can further support the global development of the game, through our competitions, through the FIFA Forward programme and through our various other initiatives, and in full dialogue with the Confederations and stakeholders.”For UEFA, though, lifting the boycott is being framed as a practical decision rather than a retreatA source familiar with the discussions told Reuters:“It’s not a UEFA defeat, rather the reality of avoiding hurting young players’ once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. The actions and insistence on change will continue.”That final sentence is perhaps the most revealing part of the development: UEFA may be stepping away from the boycott, but it does not intend to step away from its campaign for change.The pressure on Infantino hasn't gone awayInfantino's problems have now moved well beyond the original investment proposal.UEFA is among three continental confederations putting pressure on the FIFA president to resign, alongside the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF. The three regional bodies have also discussed the possibility of a vote of no confidence.Infantino is preparing to seek a fourth term in next year's FIFA presidential election and is increasingly facing the prospect of serious opposition.His position has also been weakened by the growing number of European federations withdrawing their support.Italy withdrew its backing for Infantino's re-election on Wednesday, becoming the latest federation to distance itself from him. England, Wales and Ireland had already withdrawn their support earlier this month, while Norway has called for him to step down.Romania also followed Italy on Wednesday, with the country's federation executive committee voting not to support Infantino for another term.Romanian federation president Răzvan Burleanu said:“FIFA needs today a new leader who can produce consensus and unity, inspire trust and who has the ability to bring us all together.”That leaves Infantino in a much less comfortable position than he appeared to be in before the World Cup investment controversy erupted.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sávio or Savinho? Tottenham’s £85m marquee signing scores on debut, but what is his actual name?
articles.summary: Football News: Sávio Moreira de Oliveira, formerly known as Savinho, shines on his Tottenham debut with a goal and an assist, prompting discussions about his name change and future prospects with the club.
articles.body: Sávio Moreira de Oliveira made an immediate impact on his Tottenham debut, scoring in the 82nd minute as Spurs defeated Charlton Athletic 5-1 in the Carabao Cup. The Brazilian winger had come off the bench in the 71st minute, giving him just 11 minutes on the pitch before opening his Tottenham account.There was something else that caught the eye before he even took to the pitch, though. Tottenham's new No. 17 is not wearing the name Manchester City supporters became accustomed to seeing.The player previously known as Savinho has returned to Sávio.Sávio or Savinho: what is his real name?The Brazilian's full name is Sávio Moreira de Oliveira, and Sávio is the name now appearing on the back of his Tottenham shirt.It is not the first time he has changed the name he uses on his jersey.Sávio began his career at Atlético Mineiro before moving to French side Troyes in 2022. His breakthrough came during a loan spell at Girona, where he scored 11 goals and provided 10 assists and earned his first Brazil call-up.At Girona, however, the name printed on his No. 16 shirt was Sávio.When he moved to Manchester City in 2024, that changed to Savinho.Why did he use Savinho at Manchester City?Sávio actually explained the decision himself shortly after arriving at City.The Brazilian said the change was connected to his first involvement with the Brazil national team, where he was given the name Savinho on his shirt."[My name change] is because in the national team, the first call-up they put Savinho on the shirt," he said in July 2024.He also explained the difference between how he was known by people around Girona and what appeared on his shirt there."People in Girona knew me more as Savinho, it was just written Sávio on the shirt, you know?"So I told [City] to put Savinho on the shirt and I hope it brings me luck too, this name Savinho."That meant the name Savinho became closely associated with his first season at Manchester City, where he produced 13 assists in his debut campaign in England.His second season was less productive, however. He fell out of favour under Pep Guardiola and made only 13 starts in all competitions before eventually moving on.Why has he gone back to Sávio at Tottenham?This time, the change has gone in the opposite direction.Tottenham's new signing has requested to be referred to as Sávio, with that name now printed on his No. 17 shirt.There has been no official explanation from either the club or the player specifically addressing why he has chosen to return to Sávio. What the available background does show is that this is a name he was already using before his move to Manchester City, meaning the Tottenham switch represents a return rather than an entirely new choice.The timing also gives the change a natural connection with his new chapter.Sávio has left City after one season at the club and joined Tottenham in a deal reported at £85 million ($116 million).And now, before he has even had time to settle into north London, he has already put his new name on the scoresheet.A debut that could not have gone much betterThe name change would have been an interesting detail on its own, but Sávio's first appearance has immediately given it a little more significance.After entering the game in the 71st minute, he did not take long to introduce himself. His goal came in the 82nd minute, when he cut in from the right and calmly found the bottom corner to make it 4-1 and putting his own name on the scoresheet for the first time in a Spurs shirt.Three minutes later, he appeared to have another.Sávio tried his luck again and the ball found the net after taking a heavy deflection off Ben Davies. What initially looked like a second goal for the debutant was subsequently credited to Davies instead.Sávio therefore finished the night with one goal and one assist, playing a part in Tottenham's emphatic 5-1 victory and their progression to the third round of the Carabao Cup.For a player beginning a new chapter after leaving Manchester City, it was an especially encouraging first appearance, and he did it under the name he has now chosen to carry into that chapter: Sávio.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Manchester United forced to fix new season kit after breaking little-known Premier League rule in opening match
articles.summary: Football News: Manchester United faces hiccups as they violate a Premier League kit rule in their opening match against Hull City. Discover the changes and what's next for the club.
articles.body: Manchester United have already had to make a small adjustment to their 2026-27 kit after inadvertently falling foul of a Premier League regulation in their opening game of the season.United began the campaign without a sleeve sponsor following the expiry of their agreement with DXC Technology, which had been worth around £20 million per year since 2022. But without a sponsor occupying the left sleeve, the club was required to display the Premier League badge there as well as on the right.That did not happen during Saturday's 2-0 defeat at newly promoted Hull City.What did Manchester United get wrong?United's shirts at the MKM Stadium carried the Premier League badge on the right sleeve, while the left sleeve was left blank.The Premier League's 2026-27 handbook contains 29 rules under its section on ‘Players’ Identification and Strip’, covering everything from shirt numbers and sponsorship to captain's armbands and potential kit clashes.The relevant provision is Rule M.15, which states:“The logo of the League … shall appear on the right sleeve of both home strip and alternative strip shirts.“Where the relevant strip does not bear a sponsor’s logo on the left sleeve of its shirt, a logo of the league shall appear on that sleeve as well.”Because United no longer have a sleeve sponsor, the second part of the rule applies to them.While neither the Premier League nor Manchester United commented on the issue, Daily Mail Sport understands that the club has been given a polite reminder of the requirement.The mistake will be corrected for United's first home game of the season against Ipswich Town at Old Trafford on Sunday, with the Premier League badge expected to appear on both sleeves.Why is United’s left sleeve blank?United have had a sleeve sponsor for the past eight seasons, but their agreement with DXC Technology officially ended at the conclusion of the 2025-26 campaign.The company had briefly appeared on the club's 2026-27 home shirt during the final two fixtures of last season, but that was the final outing of the partnership.When United subsequently released their new kit and promotional imagery for the 2026-27 season, the left sleeve was completely blank.The club is still searching for a new sleeve sponsor.United do retain their main shirt sponsorship with Snapdragon, in a deal worth more than £60 million per year, while Betway has a £20 million-per-season agreement covering the training kit.Until a new sleeve sponsor arrives, however, the Premier League badge has to fill that space.A rough opening day for UnitedThe kit error was a minor issue compared with what happened on the pitch.United suffered a 2-0 defeat away to newly promoted Hull, conceding both goals from set pieces and leaving manager Michael Carrick with plenty to address before another meeting with a promoted side.Captain Bruno Fernandes was particularly critical of United's performance after the final whistle."Every away game we give too much of the ball to them. In the first 20 minutes, the goalkeeper was the one with the most touches."We needed to press more, be more aggressive, and then again we need to work on set plays and not concede these types of goals. Against these types of teams, they are waiting for that moment."Carrick acknowledged that his side had shown some positive moments but said the early setback had made the match considerably harder."Yeah, some [of the game] was okay, obviously bits to improve on. It was never going to be perfect today but I think going behind and giving ourselves a lot to do makes it more difficult, probably a typical one of those games of a newly promoted team at home."You can't give them much, they've got a lot to hold on to, and then after that, we had moments, we had opportunities, we just didn't have that spark to then put the chances away or create any more."Listen, we're bitterly disappointed with the result today but it won't knock us."The United manager added:"Inside, we are hurting. The boys know we need to get better."We've lost one game and it's a bad one to lose. But it won't change anything."United will return to Old Trafford against Ipswich on Sunday, when their kit should have both Premier League badges in place.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chelsea issue explosive warning to fans after sectarian anti-Pope and anti-IRA chants heard during Fulham win
articles.summary: Football News: Chelsea FC has issued a strong warning to supporters after discriminatory sectarian chants were heard during their recent victory over Fulham. The club emphasizes a zero-tolerance policy against such behavior.
articles.body: Chelsea have warned supporters against discriminatory chanting after a section of their away following was heard singing a sectarian song during Monday's 3-2 win over Fulham at Craven Cottage.The chant, ‘Flute for 50 Pence’, includes an anti-Catholic and anti-Irish Republican line, and Chelsea moved quickly to address the incident after becoming aware of what had been sung in the away end.Chelsea issue warning to supportersAccording to the Mirror, Chelsea contacted fans who attended the west London derby with a message thanking them for their support while making clear that the club would not tolerate discriminatory chanting.The email said:"Dear supporter, Thank you for your fantastic support during our opening Premier League fixture of the season against Fulham. The whole team and manager recognised your contribution to helping secure our first win of the campaign."The passion and backing from our fans are vital in achieving a successful season, and we encourage you to continue your vocal support for the team. Following the fixture, we have received multiple reports of sectarian chanting from a small portion of those in attendance at the match."We would like to strongly remind all supporters that the club does not condone any chants which discriminate against a protected characteristic. Any supporter found guilty of this will face the strongest possible action, which could include indefinite suspension from attending all Chelsea matches and ejection from the stadium."Following previous club fines and charges for chants of this nature, and to ensure that we create a welcoming matchday experience for all, we ask supporters to take collective responsibility and remain vigilant in helping us tackle discriminatory chanting."If you witness any discriminatory language or behaviour while supporting the team, please report it to us by notifying your nearest matchday steward whilst at the game or via our dedicated reporting form."Thank you for your ongoing support throughout this season. Chelsea FC."The club's reference to previous action is significant. Chelsea were fined more than £8,000 in January 2025 after supporters sang an anti-IRA chant during a 5-1 Conference League victory over Shamrock Rovers.Why the chant has a wider historyThe song is associated with a long-standing connection between sections of Chelsea's support and Rangers, with the chant also having been used in the context of Rangers' rivalry with Celtic.Celtic have a deep historical connection with the Roman Catholic Church, which helps explain the sectarian nature of the chant and why its use has repeatedly caused disciplinary problems.The Football Association is also aware of the latest incident. There is a recent precedent for punishment: in October 2025, the FA fined Lincoln £8,500 after supporters twice directed the same anti-Pope and anti-IRA chant towards former Wrexham and Republic of Ireland player James McClean.Chelsea could therefore face disciplinary consequences of their own.Chelsea's win was overshadowed by a heated derbyThe chanting was not the only source of tension during an unusually fiery opening-day meeting between the two west London clubs.Chelsea took the lead after just one minute, with João Pedro giving Xabi Alonso the perfect start to his Premier League reign. Fulham responded through Josh King, but Chelsea restored their advantage when Morgan Rogers scored on his debut.Cole Palmer then extended Chelsea's lead shortly after half-time before another debutant, Gonzalo García, pulled one back for Fulham in the 54th minute.The hosts pushed for an equaliser but Chelsea held on for a 3-2 victory.There was another hostile moment when Enzo Fernández came off the bench. The Argentine was heavily jeered by Fulham supporters, with the reaction linked to his previous taunting of England after Argentina's World Cup victory.For Alonso, managing the emotion of the occasion was part of the challenge."[It's important] to manage in difficult moments, not to lose this emotional control. We know the Premier League is fantastic because sometimes the games are out of your hands."You don't control them, so the players on the pitch need to know how to manage it - it's as important as the tactics being right. It's a process but today we went through good moments on that and we need to carry on that."With the controversy now addressed, Chelsea turn their attention to their next competitive fixture: a second-round EFL Cup meeting with Luton Town.The League One side will travel to Stamford Bridge on Thursday, August 27, with kick-off scheduled for 7:30pm BST (12:00am IST on Friday). The match will also be a notable one for Xabi Alonso, marking his first official home game in charge of Chelsea.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Alexandre Pires leva pagonejo ao Barretão e canta com Marrone | G1
articles.standfirst: Único representante do pagode no palco Estádio, cantor levou sucessos sertanejos para nova roupagem e também revisitou clássicos da carreira na madrugada desta quinta-feira (27).
articles.summary: Alexandre Pires em Barretos apresentou o projeto Pagonejo Bão com clássicos sertanejos e a participação especial de Marrone na arena da Festa do Peão.
articles.body:
O cantor Alexandre Pires levou o projeto "Pagonejo Bão" à arena da Festa do Peão de Barretos na madrugada desta quinta-feira (27) e conquistou a turma do chapéu. O cantor ainda recebeu o sertanejo Marrone, para surpresa do público.

Único representante do pagode na programação do palco, o cantor apostou na mistura dos dois gêneros para colocar a arena para dançar.

A apresentação começou dando o tom do que o público encontraria ao longo da madrugada: muito pagode, sertanejo e sucessos conhecidos em uma nova roupagem. Logo nos primeiros minutos, Alexandre Pires levou para a arena um dos grandes hits de Jorge & Mateus, “Pode Chorar”, em uma versão que fez a galera cantar e balançar.

Alexandre Pires recebe Marrone para cantar pagonejo na Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Reprodução/BRTVMax

Na sequência, o cantor apresentou “A Gente Se Entrega”, sucesso de Rionegro & Solimões, mantendo a proposta de transformar clássicos sertanejos em pagode e aproximar dois gêneros que, apesar de diferentes, dividem espaço no coração do público brasileiro.

O público que permanecia no Parque do Peão não se decepcionou. Acompanhado por uma equipe de dançarinos e cantores, Alexandre Pires conduziu a apresentação com muita animação e interação com os fãs, em um repertório que alternava sucessos sertanejos e músicas que marcaram sua trajetória.

Alexandre Pires acompanhado por backing vocals no palco da Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

Para Barretos, o cantor preparou um repertório especial, que incluiu clássicos como “Dormi na Praça”, de Bruno & Marrone, e “Chora, Me Liga”, de João Bosco & Vinícius.

A proposta também abriu espaço para uma viagem pela história do próprio Alexandre Pires, que apresentou sucessos da época em que estava à frente do Só Pra Contrariar.

“Domingo”, “Meu Jeito de Ser”, “Essa Tal Liberdade”, “Que Se Chama Amor”, “Nosso Sonho Não É Ilusão” e “A Barata” foram algumas das músicas apresentadas.

Alexandre Pires canta sucessos sertanejos no ritmo do pagode na Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

Nas arquibancadas, camarotes e demais espaços da arena, os fãs acompanharam o ritmo e cantaram junto com o artista, que reforçou a vocação da Festa do Peão para reunir diferentes vertentes da música brasileira.

“Barretos também é do pagode. É do sertanejo. É da música brasileira.”

A apresentação seguiu justamente nessa proposta: unir os sucessos do pagode às músicas sertanejas que fazem parte da memória afetiva do público, em uma versão repaginada para o projeto Pagonejo Bão.

“Uma grande realização pra mim, que sempre curti o sertanejo, estar aqui. Hoje apresentamos para vocês o meu Pagonejo Bão.”

Alexandre Pires quebra protocolo no palco sertanejo da Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026 e leva pagode — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

Uma das surpresas da noite foi a participação do cantor Marrone, que faz dupla com Bruno.

Convidado por Alexandre Pires para subir ao palco, ele se juntou ao artista para cantar “Tentei Te Esquecer”, sucesso de Matogrosso & Mathias, além de “Agora Vai” e “Por Um Minuto”, sucessos de Bruno & Marrone. Todos, claro, em ritmo de pagode.

articles.title: FIFA World Cup’s most-hated hydration breaks could be ‘soft-launched’ in the Champions League
articles.summary: Football News: Concerns arise as ex-goalkeeper Ben Foster warns about controversial hydration breaks from the World Cup making their way into club football, potentially transforming the Champions League's match structure.
articles.body: One of the most controversial features introduced at the 2026 World Cup could have a life beyond the tournament, with former England goalkeeper Ben Foster fearing that what began as a tournament measure could eventually become part of the regular club football landscape.Hydration breaks proved hugely unpopular with sections of supporters during the World Cup, with the three-minute stoppages midway through each half disrupting the flow of matches and prompting questions over whether football was becoming too fragmented. Foster now believes the Premier League and Champions League could eventually face the same change, although the Premier League has confirmed that it will not introduce mandatory, blanket hydration breaks among its rule changes for the 2026-27 season.Why hydration breaks caused such a stirFIFA introduced mandatory three-minute hydration breaks midway through each half at the World Cup, meaning matches were effectively divided into four separate periods rather than two continuous 45-minute halves.The interruptions were criticised by players and managers who felt they affected the momentum and identity of matches, with USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino making his position clear during the tournament."I don’t like it. I only like it when the conditions are extreme. But when the conditions are good, it is unnecessary," Pochettino said.The commercial side of the decision also attracted attention because broadcasters could use the stoppages as advertising opportunities. A 30-second World Cup commercial slot on Fox Sports reportedly cost between $200,000 and $300,000, with prices reaching around $750,000 during the latter stages of the competition.The World Cup final added another controversial alteration to the traditional match format. A Super Bowl-style half-time show extended the interval to 27 minutes, exceeding the 15-minute maximum stipulated by the Laws of the Game.Foster fears football is becoming ‘quarters’Foster has played more than 550 professional matches for club and country, and he believes the physical impact of the stoppages could become particularly noticeable for older players because they have less time to remain loose and ready to resume at full intensity.Speaking exclusively on talkSPORTDrive, Foster said: "If you’re an older player it does, if you’re about 32 onwards [it will affect you]."I would like to think they have bikes in the changing room because they will have to get moving pretty quick, because you can stiffen up so quickly."But his concern goes beyond the physical effects. Foster believes the regular interruptions fundamentally alter how teams experience and manage a football match."The halves are not even 45 minutes anymore, they’re quarters. It would not surprise me if these hydration breaks crept into the Premier League," he said."It would not surprise me one little bit. Where there’s money to be made, there’s a way. They will find a reason to justify it."The league has confirmedThat prediction is not currently reflected in the Premier League's rules for the new season.World Cup’s Most-Hated Hydration Breaks Could Be ‘Soft-Launched’ in the Champions Leaguethat mandatory hydration breaks will not be introduced across matches in 2026-27. Cooling breaks can still be used when temperatures exceed 30°C (86°F), with the referee deciding before kick-off whether conditions warrant one.Why Foster thinks the Champions League could be nextFoster is nevertheless concerned that the absence of mandatory breaks in England will not necessarily stop the idea from spreading elsewhere, particularly if football discovers a financial incentive to make the interruptions part of the matchday product.He pointed to VAR as an example of how difficult it can become to reverse a change once football has invested heavily in it, regardless of how supporters feel about the system."There’s nothing we can do as football fans to stop it, they introduced VAR and every single one of us hates it," Foster said."I could do away with VAR tomorrow, but they won’t now because they invested so much money into it."He believes the Champions League could be where the concept is introduced gradually before becoming more widespread."They will do a soft launch in the Champions League, for example, you watch. Clubs will say ‘oh we get an extra million quid'."Foster also believes the World Cup breaks have already changed the way some teams approach their matches, with coaches and players able to treat each interruption almost like a reset point."Teams have been approaching games differently because it’s in quarters, so you can break it down into the four parts. But I hate it."His concerns echo those voiced by other figures in the game. England manager Thomas Tuchel has previously said the stoppages "interrupt and change the identity of a football match", while UEFA has ruled out introducing the same mandatory system in European competition.For now, then, Foster's prediction remains just that: a warning about where he believes football could be heading. The Premier League has specifically rejected mandatory hydration breaks, but his broader concern is that once a change creates a commercial opportunity, football's authorities may eventually find a reason to make it permanent.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Everything Mike Elko said during Wednesday's Aggie Football Hour
articles.summary: Here is everything Texas A&M coach Mike Elko said during Wednesday's first Aggie Football Hour ahead of the 2026 season opener vs. Missouri State.
articles.body:
Texas A&M's 2026 season opener vs. Missouri State is just nine days away, which means coach Mike Elko , entering his third year at the helm, made his way back to Rudy's Country Store and BBQ on Harvey Road in College Station for the Aggie Football Hour, as the Aggies begin in-season practices with their sights set on starting the 2026 season 1-0 before hosting Arizona State in Week 2.

Through 16 preseason practices, it became abundantly clear that redshirt junior quarterback Marcel Reed has improved, especially his deep-ball accuracy, which was on full display during the last two scrimmages, connecting with star junior wide receiver Mario Craver for a 50-yard touchdown, while his growing chemistry with Alabama transfer wideout Isaiah Horton is even more critical.

While Reed's improvement, combined with four new starters along the offensive line, will "make or break" the Aggies' chances at making it back to the College Football Playoff for a second straight season, among the 17 transfer portal additions, Texas A&M 's defense, especially the secondary, looks like the team's primary strength outside of the wide receiver corps.

Mike Elko's is a straight shooter, and while he is also one of the funnier head coaches in the country, Wednesday's Aggie Football Hour was all business ahead of the season opener, focused on recapping the preseason and what to expect once the 2026 roster finally takes the field.

Here is everything Mike Elko said on Wednesday night.

Mike Elko was the best fit for College Station

"That's the program you want to build. You earn every opportunity that Texas A&M has given you. A scholarship, an opportunity to be part of this great university, to be a part of it's history."

For the newcomers, walking down the tunnel into Kyle Field will be something to remember

"We've got kids that have transferred from high-profile schools, but until you come walking down that tunnel in the opener on a Saturday night, and you feel it, you haven't done it." "It's completely different."

"We've got kids that have transferred from high-profile schools, but until you come walking down that tunnel in the opener on a Saturday night, and you feel it, you haven't done it."

"Ultimately you want this to be a place where people feel like they're given a platform to grow. If they feel like they're given the platform to grow, then what happens at somepoint is they grow to the next phase of their career."

Being an SEC head coach requires selflessness

"I always wanted to be a guy that felt as though he was doing right by all of the people in his building, not just what was in my best interest or what was best for me and Texas A&M."

Every player on the 2026 roster has received over 1,000 reps this offseason

"There are close to 2,000 reps between last season and September 5th. To each kid, they're probably getting somewhere around 1,000 to 1,100 plays."

Mike Elko on Texas A&M's 2026 linebacker room

"It's a good group. It's obviously great to have Daymion Sanford back out there… I think Ray Coney has had a phenomenal summer. "Then you got Noah Mikhail and Jordan Lockhart, I think ready to get out there."

"It's a good group. It's obviously great to have Daymion Sanford back out there… I think Ray Coney has had a phenomenal summer.

"Then you got Noah Mikhail and Jordan Lockhart, I think ready to get out there."

College football is not for the faint of heart

"It's a long, grueling, physical sport… you got to get used to that. You've got to embrace it a little bit. You've got to embrace the fact that you've got to be able to compete at a really, really high level when you don't feel your absolute best all the time."

No one in the building will be taking Arizona State lightly

"People lose sight of the fact that Arizona State is a top-25 team that beat Texas Tech last year. So, we have nine [conference games] plus another one."

Mike Elko on the annual Celebrity Softball Game

"It was a blast… the more we do it, the more we can grow it. I think it's cool to be doing things like that in the Bryan-College Station community."

Contact/Follow us @AggiesWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Texas A&M news, notes and opinions. Follow Cameron on X: @CameronOhnysty.

articles.title: Who is in the Conference League draw and who is in each pot?
articles.summary: Our Ask Me Anything team explains the details for Friday's league phase draw for the 2026-27 Conference League
articles.body:
The league phase draw for the 2026-27 Conference League takes place on Friday, 28 August at 12:00 BST in Monaco .

The draw will take place in a joint event alongside the Europa League, with the Conference League expected to take place as the second of the two draws.

As with both the Champions League and Europa League, the Conference League will consist of 36 clubs. Scottish side Hearts are the only team confirmed so far, with the other 35 to be confirmed on Thursday.

Unlike the other two competitions, each team will play six league phase matches instead of eight.

For the draw, the 36 teams will be placed into six pots, with pot one being the highest-ranked and six being the lowest. The pot placements are based on the club's Uefa club coefficient ranking from the five-season period ending at the conclusion of the 2025-26 season.

Each team will face one team from each of the six pots and cannot face a team from the same country as themselves.

The teams who finish in the top eight places will qualify for the Conference League's round of 16. Those between ninth and 24th place will enter the play-off knockout round. The 12 teams ranked between 25th and 36th place will exit the competition when the league phase is concluded.

Hearts are the only club to have so far qualified for the Conference League's league phase, with their qualifying round match taking place a day earlier than the rest of the fixtures.

The highest pot they can qualify for is pot two, although it is more likely that the Jam Tarts will drop down to a lower pot.

As one of the highest-ranked clubs that could enter the league phase of the Conference League, Rangers are guaranteed to enter pot one if they qualify. Benfica, Atalanta and Braga would also be among the clubs to also enter pot one, should they qualify.

It is mathematically possible for Brighton and Hove Albion to enter the top pot. However, they would need at least five of the 21 teams who could qualify that have a higher club rating to not reach the league phase.

Due to their club coefficient ratings, Motherwell and Hibernian would enter one of the lower pots if they qualify.

Shamrock Rovers, of the Republic of Ireland, would be in a higher pot than the majority of the British clubs currently in qualifying. Only Rangers and Brighton would rank above them.

Larne, of Northern Ireland, are also a higher-ranked team than Motherwell and Hibernian.

Which teams are in this season's Conference League?
